Thanks, Dylan — quick pass attached (offer_page_copy_comments.docx). Notes: 

1) Hero line: current "Low-latency LLM inference at 5–20ms per token" is risky. We should change to something like: "High-performance LLM inference optimized for low-latency production workloads" and then include an example latency footnote ("Example benchmark on c6i.4xlarge with 512 tokens — see benchmarks page") instead of a universal claim.

2) "Enterprise-grade guarantees" — fine for marketing, but can't be framed as an SLA. Replace with "Designed for high-availability production deployments".

3) Security/compliance callouts: we can say "SOC 2 ready with VPC/private deployment options" but remove anything that suggests we host compliance reports on behalf of customers.

4) Value props: tighten the bullets to emphasize what customers can do (predictable cost controls, rollout policies, unified API) rather than making absolute performance guarantees.

I'll add inline suggestions in the docx. I did not change the SKU names — Ben, can you confirm the tier names and whether "Burst" pricing should be shown on the public Offer or only in Private Offer footnotes?

+Marissa
Senior Director, Product Marketing
Redwood Inference

Quick pricing update: attached SKU_pricing_map_v2.xlsx has the corrected public tier prices and a separate tab with Private Offer guidance. Summary:
- Starter (s1): pay-as-you-go / $0.XX per token equivalent (public)
- Standard (s2): reserved baseline + burst (public + sample pricing)
- Dedicated (d1): reserved capacity; list price shows monthly baseline only — note that private offer discounts are handled via BOT/PO flow.

Ben's recommendation: keep burst language out of hero and put a short sentence in pricing footnote: "Burst capacity subject to availability; contact sales for private offer pricing." That prevents overpromising and keeps public listing clean.

I also swapped the SKU names to the shorthand we use in billing (s1/s2/d1) so mapping is easier for finance. Deal id RDW-4558 is the Acme POC — they're exploring Dedicated for high-throughput analytics.

Attachment: SKU_pricing_map_v2.xlsx

Hi Dylan/Marissa —

Thanks for the early share. Quick checklist from Marketplace compliance & PM teams: 
1) Hero claim: prefer conservative language. Use benchmarking examples rather than blanket numbers.
2) Security statements: include the SOC 2 readiness phrasing you proposed, and ensure any "data residency" lines map to the Regions metadata (we'll validate at submission).
3) AMI: include the AMI ID pattern and ensure bucket naming/docs are present in the seller assets.
4) Pricing: Marketplace will surface public list prices only. Any private discounts should be placed in the Private Offer section and referenced in the Offer description as "Contact us for private offer pricing" — do not publish both public and private discounted prices.

I've added internal comments on the preview: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/offer/preview/12345 (preview link, expires in 48 hours).

If you can update the hero and the pricing footnote, please resend and I'll route to PM for final acceptance. Also attach the AMI tagging doc in the listing assets before submission.

DocuSign: I'll also send the marketplace listing NDA via DocuSign (DocuSign: 0A1B2C3D4E) — sign and return to get the marketplace listing workflow unlocked.

Best,
